### Observed differences

- The largest change concerns A32 and A33. In the earlier window each appeared in about 52 in 100 traces, and they always appeared together (co-occurring in 52.5% of traces, never one without the other); in the later window each appears in only about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC004, OCC005, REL026]
- A27 moved the opposite way: from 48 in 100 traces to all 200. A26 now routes to A27 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, where previously about 47 in 100 went to A27 and roughly 26 in 100 each went to A33 and A32; A27 is followed by A28 in about 99 in 100 cases. [OCC003, DIR002, DIR003, REL017, REL020]
- The surroundings of A32/A33 changed accordingly. Previously A40 preceded A32/A33 in about 52 in 100 traces, and A32/A33 preceded A28; in the later window A40 precedes A32/A33 in essentially no traces and instead precedes A27 in about 99 in 100. A27 and A32/A33 were mutually exclusive before and remain so afterwards, with A27 now on the "always" side. [REL023, REL024, REL025, REL027, REL028, REL021, REL022]
- A06 became about three times as common: 7 in 100 traces before, 29 in 100 after (14 vs 58 traces). Its outgoing transitions shifted from a spread over A46, A15 and A16 (14–21% each) to mainly A19 (55%) and A20 (27%), and the share of A40's outgoing transitions going to A06 rose from under 1% to about 25%. [OCC002, DIR001, DIR006]
- In the later window A06 sits inside the main flow: it precedes A26, A27 and A28 in about 25 in 100 traces each, follows A14 and A40, is followed by A19 one position later in about 96 in 100 observed pairs, and reaches A26 about three positions later. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL007, LAG001, LAG002]
- A02 fell from 11 in 100 to 2 in 100 traces. [OCC001]
- Smaller consistent shifts: A26 to A28 is now almost always two positions apart (98%, previously split between two and three), and A13 no longer co-occurs with A32/A33 (22% to about 0.5%) while preceding A27 in 54% of traces (was 25%). [LAG006, REL008, REL009, REL010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the part of the process executing A32 and A33 — previously run in about half the cases, always jointly, between A40/A26 and A28 — is no longer executed in the later window, with A27 now running in every case in that role (A40 before A27, A27 before A28, and A26 routing almost exclusively to A27). A related possibility is that A06 now regularly takes a place in this flow, appearing after A14/A40 and before A26/A27/A28 and leading to A19. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR002, REL017, REL020, REL023, REL026, REL002, REL003, LAG001]

Supporting signs: participation, routing and relational evidence all point the same way — A32/A33 fell from about 52 in 100 traces to none while A27 rose to all traces, A26's outgoing share moved from A32/A33 to A27, A40's precedence flipped from A32/A33 to A27, and the A26→A28 distance concentrating at two positions matches A27 now always lying between them. The 53 qualifying items far exceed the roughly 0.75 expected without a change, and the key routing items rest on about 200 observations per window. [DIR002, REL021, REL022, LAG006]

Limitations: the later-window behaviour of A32 and A33 themselves rests on a single observed trace each, so any statement about what exactly replaced their outgoing edges or positions is weakly supported. The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is sampling: with 200-trace windows, variant frequencies can shift substantially without any change, and many of these items describe the same underlying trace behaviour rather than independent confirmations — although a fall from 105 in 200 to 1 in 200, together with the matching rerouting of A26 and A40, is difficult to attribute to sampling alone. [DIR004, DIR005, POS002, POS003, LAG007]
